original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be a locally nilpotent K-derivation or K-E-derivation. Here locally nilpotent means that for each a in A there exists m >= 1 such that delta^m(a) = 0. For every choice of left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A and every idempotent e in delta(I), meaning e^2 = e, must the corresponding left, right, or two-sided ideal generated by e be contained in delta(I)?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.7(B) (the locally nilpotent part of the "Idempotent Conjecture"); the paper presents it as the weaker idempotent-only form of the broader LNED conjecture, and in the algebraic-over-K case it is equivalent to Conjecture 1.6 by Theorem 1.8.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the characteristic-zero hypothesis on K, the ambient K-algebra A, the locally nilpotent hypothesis on delta, the choice between K-derivations and K-E-derivations, the quantification over left/right/two-sided ideals I, the idempotent condition e^2=e with e in delta(I), and the desired containment of the corresponding generated ideal inside delta(I).
missing_details: The nearest official target in the paper is not the full LNED conjecture itself, but Conjecture 1.7(B), the weaker "Idempotent Conjecture" for the locally nilpotent case.
A K-E-derivation should be defined explicitly: it is a K-linear map delta = I_A - phi for some K-algebra endomorphism phi of A; equivalently, delta(ab) = delta(a)b + a delta(b) - delta(a)delta(b).

The paper packages the left/right/two-sided cases using a parameter theta in {left, right, two-sided}; the conclusion is that the principal theta-ideal (e)_theta generated by e is contained in delta(I).
If you want the question fully stand-alone in noncommutative language, you should spell out the principal theta-ideal generated by e, e.g. left/right/two-sided according to the chosen theta.
The paper explicitly situates this statement as a weaker consequence of the LNED conjecture and not as the LNED conjecture itself; that relation should be noted to stay paper-faithful.
If you also mention the algebraic-case equivalent formulation, you must define a theta-Mathieu subspace and make clear that "for all sufficiently large m" is the meaning of m >> 0.
No commutativity assumption on A should be added, since the conjecture is posed for general K-algebras.
refined_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be a locally nilpotent K-derivation or K-E-derivation of A, where a K-E-derivation means a K-linear map of the form delta = I_A - phi for some K-algebra endomorphism phi of A (equivalently, delta(ab) = delta(a)b + a delta(b) - delta(a)delta(b)), and locally nilpotent means that for every a in A there exists m >= 1 such that delta^m(a) = 0. Fix theta in {left, right, two-sided}. If I is a theta-ideal of A and e in delta(I) is an idempotent, must the principal theta-ideal (e)_theta generated by e be contained in delta(I)?
equivalent_formulation: If A is algebraic over K, this is equivalent to asking whether for every locally nilpotent K-derivation or K-E-derivation delta of A and every theta-ideal I of A, the image delta(I) is a theta-Mathieu subspace of A; that is, whenever a^m lies in delta(I) for all m >= 1, then b a^m lies in delta(I) for all sufficiently large m if theta = left, a^m c lies in delta(I) for all sufficiently large m if theta = right, and b a^m c lies in delta(I) for all sufficiently large m if theta = two-sided, for all b,c in A.
justification: Although the paper first raises the broader image problem and then states the full LNED conjecture, your draft does not ask whether delta(I) is a theta-Mathieu subspace; it asks only for the idempotent-generated ideal containment. That is exactly the content of Conjecture 1.7(B) in Section 1 of the accessible arXiv text. The same nearby context supplies the definition of K-E-derivation and the definition of theta-Mathieu subspace, and Theorem 1.8 gives the paper-explicit equivalence between Conjecture 1.7(B) and the LNED conjecture when A is algebraic over K.
